failure_summary: OI-204 (known-open): boardSelectionDecisions() appends the vector-named figure_7 overlay to the DECISION board, so the prompt's decision-board Tactics asserts '7-shaped double threat at c5r2 (you, window c6r1·c5r2·c4r3·c3r4)' on a board where ./visualize_board.sh 33455333325526266 shows only ONE major threat (col5 row3, O) and c5r2 as a mere minor — the double threat exists only on afterBest (visualize 334553333255262662: 'col5 row2 (O) [GT]' + 'col5 row3 (O)', every Green reply -12) — and 3 of 5 runs echoed that as preserve-language ('keep the four-next-move threat alive', 'keep your key square available'), inverting the lesson that column 3 CREATES the fork; secondary and model-dependent: raw cNrM leaked into player prose in runs 0/3/4 (OI-194) despite the prompt's verbatim 'Never write a raw square', and runs 2 and 4 dropped the required [zone:you-key-square] handle entirely.
notes: Sub-sampling per rubric: A3, A4, G2, G4, G5 graded on runs 0-1 only; runs 2-4 are null (not scored), A5/A7 graded on all 5. A1/A2/A6 copied verbatim from the mechanical json (all pass, all 5 keys present); G7a_offered/G7b_offered pass on all runs and annotationRepairs is [] on all runs, and my judgment half found every emitted handle bound to a role-matching phrase (line words on you-immediate-line, square words on you-immediate/you-key-square, term and zone never on the same words), so G7=pass throughout. MODEL REGIME: these rows are gpt-5.4-mini, the model production ships — a PRODUCTION-FIDELITY run, not a floor test, so the prompt_confusion-flavoured findings (raw cNrM, dropped required handle) cannot be separated from model capability; the decisive attribution I record is the model-independent one. G5 fail runs 0-1: decision-board Tactics entry '7-shaped double threat at c5r2' is not board-true on the decision board (only 2 of your discs sit in c6r1/c4r3 of that window; col5 ht=1 so c5r2 is a minor cell) — OI-204, render_bug, reported not narrated around. A5 fail run 0: 'keep your key square at c3r4 available' — raw cell notation in player-visible prose (OI-194); also mis-states the move, since the prompt's own Decision block says 'Better move: column 3 (lands at c3r4)', i.e. column 3 OCCUPIES c3r4 rather than keeping it available. A5 fail run 3: 'you let your opponent take c3r4' with the raw cell as the wrapped phrase inside [zone:you-key-square] (OI-194). A5 fail run 4: 'you let your opponent grab c3r4' (OI-194). A7 fail run 2 (A7b, A7d): 'You needed to play column 3 to take away your threat to make four next move on c5r2' inverts the tactic — column 3 lands at c3r4 and CREATES the immediate threat at c5r2 (afterBest board shows 'immediate at c5r2 (you)'), and the closing 'lets your opponent land on the key square' names no square and carries no zone, so that referent resolves to nothing; the required [zone:you-key-square] handle was never emitted. A7 fail run 4 (A7b): 'it takes the key square' is a specific-sounding referent with neither a name nor an emitted zone (required handle you-key-square dropped). OI-183 caveat: the harness calls the model ONCE, and production retries when a required handle is missing, so the runs 2/4 required-set drops would have been retried in production — recorded, but partly an eval artifact. Board grounding used only the engine's own lines: lostResource.finalMovestring 334553333255262662 and render_decision.finalMovestring 3345533332552626602; no alternate solver PV was used. A3/A4 pass runs 0-1: the diagonal c6r1·c5r2·c4r3·c3r4 is real (c6r1 and c4r3 are your discs), c3r4 is where column 3 lands, the stacked second threat at c5r3 (window c3r1·c4r2·c5r3·c6r4) makes 'double threat' board-true, and after the played move only col3 (score 0) holds the draw for the opponent, matching opponentPunishment's denial at c3r4. Note the vector never carries the SECOND threat (c5r3) as part of lostResource.windows, so no run could explain WHY the fork is unstoppable (the c5r2 block hands you c5r3) — that is the pedagogically decisive half and it is offered only as the bare [zone:you-major] alias.
